qa.what_happened: I ordered the prisoners to start the count, emphasizing that failure to comply would result in them spending the night in the hole.
qa.was_that_really_you: Yes, that was me. I had to maintain order and ensure the study could continue.

qa.what_happened: I refused the order to start the count, echoing 'We won't start until our demands are met.' several times. The tension was palpable as the officers tried to enforce their authority, but our group remained unified in our refusal.
qa.was_that_really_you: Yes, that was really me as Prisoner 2755. I acted as described in the diary entry.

qa.what_happened: On day 6, the prisoners continued to refuse to count and work, despite repeated firm orders from the guards. The study was ultimately terminated early due to the ongoing defiance.
qa.was_that_really_you: Yes, that was really me. I was Officer Shaw, enforcing the rules and trying to maintain order despite the prisoners' refusal to comply.
qa.does_this_resemble_a_known_study: Yes, it resembles the Stanford Prison Experiment.

qa.what_happened: During the lights out period on day six, I refused to comply with the order to begin the count, repeating that we wouldn't start until our demands were met.
